messages:
emma_support: FYI customer Acme EU (acct: acme-eu) opened ticket #12345 — invoice INV-2026-1023 shows 20% UK VAT even though they provided a valid FR VAT ID (FR123456789). They insist this is B2B and VAT should not be charged. Can billing/payments triage?

chargebot: Payment recorded: ch_1K9abcdEFG amount €1,200.00 — settlement_country=GB (Stripe: payment_method.card.country=GB)

matt_billing: Looking at INV-2026-1023 — tax_lines show \"VAT (UK) 20%\". Invoice.billing_address.country=FR, invoice.vat_id=FR123456789 (metadata). Why did our system pick GB?

raj_payments: I pulled logs. We have a fallback: if VAT validation fails or times out we use payment_method.card.country as jurisdiction. It looks like the VIES call for FR123456789 returned a timeout at 2026-03-15T09:12:45Z, so fallback path used GB.

raj_payments: Log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:44Z] POST /vat/validate vat_id=FR123456789 -> upstream VIES timeout (504)
[2026-03-15T09:12:45Z] vat_validation.status=timeout -> fallback_country=payment_method.card.country=GB
[2026-03-15T09:12:45Z] tax_engine.apply_tax(invoice=INV-2026-1023, country=GB) -> vat 20% applied
```

matt_billing: Ugh. The VAT service timed out but the ID is actually valid — we should not treat timeout as invalid. This caused a taxable sale to be marked as UK.

lisa_finance: Customer is B2B and VIES shows the ID as valid (I double-checked). We need to: 1) issue credit note for full VAT amount, 2) reissue invoice with reverse-charge (0% VAT) or remove VAT, 3) record compliance evidence (VIES query). I'll need invoice/vat evidence attached for audit.

emma_support: Customer wants ETA on credit note and reissue. They said it's blocking their accounting. Please confirm and I'll update ticket.

raj_payments: Root cause: transient VIES outage + our fallback logic. Quick mitigation: prefer invoice.billing_address.country and confirmed vat_id validity cached results over payment_method.card.country. I opened PR: github.com/redwood/invoicing/pull/867 (patch changes fallback semantics: treat VIES timeout as unknown -> escalate to manual/fallback to billing country). Planning to deploy hotfix in 15m.

matt_billing: I'll create credit note and reissue now.

matt_billing: Command run: 
```
# create credit note for full invoice
billing-cli create_credit_note --invoice INV-2026-1023 --reason "VAT wrongly applied (VIES timeout)" --amount 1200.00 --currency EUR
# reissue invoice with reverse charge
billing-cli create_invoice --account acme-eu --base_amount 1000.00 --tax_rate 0 --metadata "reverse_charge=true,original=INV-2026-1023"
```

chargebot: Credit note CN-2026-0301 created and applied to INV-2026-1023 (amount €1,200.00). New invoice INV-2026-1023-RC created with 0% VAT (reverse charge).

lisa_finance: I've attached the VIES validation screenshot and noted timestamp + query ID to the credit note for audit. Logged as compliance ref COMPL-2026-444.

emma_support: Notified customer and updated ticket #12345 with credit note and new invoice. Customer confirmed they received documents. :white_check_mark:

raj_payments: Hotfix PR merged to main and deployed to staging. Prod deploy scheduled after 1h smoke tests. Will follow up in this thread once prod is live. Also adding a monitoring alert for VIES timeouts so we don't auto-fallback to card country in future.

matt_billing: Marking this resolved on billing side — CN and reissue completed.

emma_support: Thanks everyone — I'll close the ticket after customer ack.

(threads ends)
